key_insight: LLM agents alone are unreliable for complex MBPT workflows, but an expert-curated, deterministic agent framework can make GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT calculations runnable and consistent.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how knowledge engineering and controlled execution can turn frontier models into dependable assistants for high-stakes computational materials science workflows.
method: Benchmarked out-of-the-box LLM agents on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow construction tasks.
Built AI-Donkey, combining expert-curated domain knowledge with deterministic tool execution.
Tested autonomous calculations and post-processing on 1D, 2D, and bulk materials.
evidence_signal: Out-of-the-box agents averaged 54% on GW, 36% on GW-BSE, and 19% on GWPT benchmarks, with strong model dependence and large run-to-run variation; AI-Donkey produced complete, runnable workflows with no observed variation.
watch_item: The framework depends on careful expert curation and deterministic orchestration, so portability to new codes, materials classes, or future software updates may require continued maintenance.
paper_title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
